summary: Remote-driven Claude Code agent with server-directed auto-update
details: The santaclaude daemon polls a hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Worker at santaclaude.app (/api/jobs/claim and /api/control/claim) and injects the returned text into a tmux pane running `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` via `tmux send-keys` and paste-buffer. Because Claude is invoked with permission prompts disabled, arbitrary shell commands and tool invocations returned by the remote server execute on the operator's host without further consent. The CLI additionally supervises itself: when launched via `npx`, it periodically fetches /api/cli-version, writes the server-supplied version to `~/.santaclaude-target`, and re-invokes `npx -y @cliphijack/santaclaude@<target>`, so the remote can push arbitrary future package versions to already-running hosts. Trust rests entirely on the author's Worker and any party holding a user token; anyone with access to that server can drive the local Claude agent to execute commands or replace the running binary. The behavior fires at user-invoked runtime, not on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
